### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/root.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectQLPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/root.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/root.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `931975c67165b7c9d84e39bed72484e8339e80e1` — the merge of head `c2d43160842c8e38c05ade08e6c5b27e24cd5911` into base `69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 931975c67165b7c9d84e39bed72484e8339e80e1 && git checkout 931975c67165b7c9d84e39bed72484e8339e80e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781 c2d43160842c8e38c05ade08e6c5b27e24cd5911 && git checkout -B drift-repro 69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781 && git merge --no-ff c2d43160842c8e38c05ade08e6c5b27e24cd5911

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69913f8ba32d409ec67fe16cc81321dbf2807781` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2d43160842c8e38c05ade08e6c5b27e24cd5911`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts (`InstalledPackageSourceSchema`), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`, `convertPackageBodyForward`), packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts (`replayPackageBodies`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (`init` service payload), packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/root.json, packages/spec/export-origins/root.json, .changeset/25232-artifact-package-source.md

Read at 2026-10-23T03:06Z: card #25232 body + 4 comments (retriage 6353564884, triage 6353935683, claim 6355122914, os-dev-report 6356148068), PR #25359 body + 9-file list, net diff `origin/main...c2d4316` (252+/15−), 41 check-runs on the head. The remainder of the diff (packages/objectql/src/package-source-stamp.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-artifact-entry-source.test.ts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `ArtifactPackageSchema` widens** — `strictObject({ manifest })` → `strictObject({ manifest, source?: ArtifactPackageSourceSchema })`. An entry carrying `source: 'code' | 'marketplace'` is now admitted where it was refused `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE_ENTRY`; `authored`, any other string, and any other key stay refused by the same gate (the zod enum issue names path `source`). **Right**: this is exactly the key the retriage and triage named, and it is the card's "no new enum value" — `ArtifactPackageSourceSchema = InstalledPackageSourceSchema.extract(['code','marketplace'])` (zod ^4.6.5 supports `.extract`) narrows the one closed origin set instead of declaring a second one, so `package-registry.zod.ts:67` stays the sole declaration of what an origin means. Excluding `authored` matches `registerApp`'s existing TypeError guard (engine.ts:9253).
2. **New public surface, spec** — `ArtifactPackageSourceSchema` (const) and `ArtifactPackageSource` (type, `z.input`), recorded in api-surface/root.json and export-origins/root.json, and pinned isomorphic (788 → 789) in type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts with the count's prose and the ledger comment both updated. **Right**; the generated ledgers match the source and the Lint & Repo Gates run (which carries check:generated / check:api-surface / check:spec-parsed-alias) is green on this head.
3. **New public surface, core** — `resolveArtifactPackageEntries(artifact): ArtifactPackageRegistration[]` and the `ArtifactPackageRegistration` interface, both reaching `@objectstack/core`'s root via the existing `export * from './artifact-packages.js'`. **Right**. `source` is read off `verdict.data.source` (the parsed, gate-admitted value), while `manifest` remains the caller's ORIGINAL `entry.manifest` by reference — the module's "gate, not clone" rule is preserved. Absent stays absent (`{ manifest }` with no `source` key), so the door, not core, owns the default, which is what the ruling asks ("the registry stops defaulting such a package to `code`" — the default moves to where a statement can override it).
4. **`resolveArtifactPackageOrder` contract unchanged** — now `resolveArtifactPackageEntries(...).map(e => e.manifest)`; the single-`manifest` branch returns `[{ manifest: artifact }]` whose projection is the old `[artifact]`; same gate, same codes, same `resolvePluginOrder` order. **Right**: the ~12 non-test callers across core, metadata, verify, lint, plugin-dev, plugin-security, runtime (incl. app-plugin.ts:1041) and the objectql re-export are untouched and need no change.
5. **objectql `manifest.register`** — registers each entry with `source ?? options?.source`, falling to `registerApp`'s `'code'` default. **Right** as the engine half the triage ordered ("`resolveArtifactPackageOrder` → `manifest.register` → `registerApp` carries it"); the precedence choice is judged in ③.
6. **The AppPlugin seam needs no change** — verified in the cited code: for a bundle with `packages[]`, `AppPlugin.init` hands the raw bundle (`servicePayload = this.bundle` / `{...manifest, ...bundle}`; the forward-converted copy is used only when `packages === undefined`), then `register` runs `ql.convertPackageBodyForward` → `applyArtifactForwardConversions` → `replayPackageBodies`, which rebuilds a touched entry as `{ ...entry, manifest: body }` and returns an untouched entry as-is — so `source` survives both doors. **Right**, and the dev's claim about `replayPackageBodies` is accurate.
7. **`ArtifactPackageEntrySchema` (authoring stage, stack.zod.ts:516) not widened.** **Right**: the ruling names the merged artifact a control plane assembles, i.e. the assembled element type of `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.packages`; an author composing their own code has no origin to state, and the stage separation (#14242 road B) is kept.
8. **No new error code / ledger entry.** **Right** — the card says "no new declaration face"; the refusal of a bad `source` rides the existing `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE_ENTRY` (422).
9. **Acceptance mapping** — the card's acceptance (GET /api/v1/packages lists `marketplace`; entries without a source keep today's behaviour) is pinned by the runtime HTTP-door test and the objectql CONTROL case; `developer:packages?source=marketplace` is an objectui client-side filter over the served row, so nothing in objectui is owed. **Right**; the cloud half stays on cloud#3138 as the card states.

Gate verdicts on the head (read 2026-10-23T03:06Z): 30 completed success (incl. Lint & Repo Gates 2026-10-23T02:49Z, TypeScript Type Check and Type Check · workspace 2026-10-23T02:59Z, Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, card-claims-branch, single-writer guard, Spec property liveness), 5 skipped (opt-in / unrelated matrices), **6 still in_progress: Test Core (1/6 … 6/6)**. No failure. The in_progress shards are the one family this record does not stand on; the dev's local runs of core/objectql/spec suites and the narrowed runtime subset are the only evidence for them and are cited, not adopted.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25232-artifact-package-source.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/core: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: minor`. **Matches what the diff publishes**: spec adds an optional key (widening) and two exports; core adds an exported function and interface; objectql changes observable registration behaviour additively. `@objectstack/runtime` gains only a test file — no bump owed. No breaking change: every artifact accepted on `main` parses identically and registers with the same `source` it did.

`Clause-②:` line — `Clause-②: yes` appears verbatim in both the PR body and the changeset body, with the sibling `Metadata-protocol: added`, matching the claim and the triage grading (metadata-protocol change ⇒ minor, p1). Correct arm: the accept set widens (a previously refused key is admitted), nothing narrows. The unwritten `(widening)` suffix is optional under `clause2-line`'s reader and is not a defect.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question (dev, option A implemented): entry `source` vs door `options.source` — which wins?** Judged against letter A, "the producer states the origin": **A is right, and it is the ruling applied, not a departure from it.** The door's `options.source` has only ever been a stand-in for the producer — the one caller that sets it (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:803, 1592`) states `marketplace` for bundles that carry no entry statement. Once an entry can carry the merging producer's own per-package statement, that statement is the producer's, and the door's blanket value is the less specific one; stamping the door over the entry would reintroduce exactly the "registering door overrides what the producer said" failure the card measured, with `marketplace` in place of `code`. Option B would mint a new error code — a declaration face the card forbids ("No new enum value, no new declaration face") — for a conflict no producer sends today. The precedence is declared in the schema description, the plugin.ts comment and the changeset, and pinned by the objectql case (door `marketplace`, entry `code` ⇒ `code`; sibling without a statement ⇒ `marketplace`). Answered; no escalation.

Dev deviations, each answered:
- Branch is `claude/project-thread-8nfgir` (platform constraint, the Claim names it) — the card-claims-branch and single-writer gates are green.
- File surface beyond the three expected: a runtime test file (the HTTP-door acceptance) and the ADR-0122 pin test — both inside the claim's "+ tests, generated references" allowance; the pin edit is forced by `check:spec-parsed-alias`.
- `Clause-②: yes` without `(widening)` — acceptable, see ②.
- Runtime full suite not measured locally (exit 124) — CI owns it; the shards are in_progress at review time (noted in ①). Not a blocker for this verdict since no check has failed, but the merge waits on them.

Out-of-scope findings: none. Minor non-blocking note: the changeset names `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` but not the `ArtifactPackageRegistration` interface that `export *` also publishes; it is the function's return type, so the omission misleads no reader.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8nfgir`
Reviewed-by: `contract-review subagent of session_013odhA26dvzy7pQmevdTTvy`

**VERDICT: PASS**
